correctness.rationale: Choose a generic intrinsic cocharacter whose ambient weights are pairwise distinct. The Grassmannian fixed points are all coordinate (N-d-1)-planes. The toric fixed points are exactly coordinate points indexed by vertices of conv(A). For a coordinate Grassmannian fixed plane L_S, nonempty projective torus-stable intersection with X_A contains a fixed point, so L_S lies on the Chow divisor exactly when S contains a vertex index. Hence the fixed-locus count is C(N,d+1)-C(N-v,N-d-1). Projective C* Euler localization proves the formula; additivity gives the complement formula. Boundary q=N-d-1>=1 is explicit, and binomial zero conventions cover v large enough that no disjoint S exists.

value.rationale: The Chow divisor is the canonical Grassmannian hypersurface encoding a projective variety and is a central object in elimination theory. For projective toric embeddings, its degree and equation can depend sensitively on normalized volume, triangulations, and secondary-polytope structure. The theorem shows that a global topological invariant behaves in the opposite way: it depends only on N, d, and the number of polytope vertices. The Veronese specialization has a universal one-fixed-point deficit, while Segre embeddings have the full ambient Grassmannian Euler characteristic. This is a natural all-family invariant, not a parameter slice or a recomputation of known degree data.
